reasoning: Both groups put a mandatory answer line at the top of the editable skill, so I merged them into one STEP 0 edit built on the failure version, which has the Type | Evidence | Check fields and the title+name, quote, plural and letter-count checks. From the success version I kept two things: the note that this one line also serves as the strategic block's check line (so the agent writes only one), and a pointer to the Rule 2 exception for 'the <part of speech> in "phrase"'. Without that pointer the clue-word substitution test would contradict that exception. All five failure edits stay as written: STEP 0, the real-people-list replace, the half-compound Rule 4 replace, the Rule 2 'of this state/city' replace, and the Rule 3 archive-dump note. The success edits cover patterns the failure edits do not, so I kept them, trimmed to save length: four short Rule 1 clue-type bullets (definition/glossary headword, shared-word, translation, 'title held by A, B & C') and two Rule 2 bullets (the quoted-phrase part-of-speech exception and the pronoun-in-phrase slot). I kept the deletion of the redundant 'Put only the bare answer...' bullet, since STEP 0 now says it, so net length stays flat. No edit touches the SLOW_UPDATE block or the substance of Rule 3's verbatim override. The 'no middle initial' idea stays out and no task-specific gold answers are embedded.

edits.content:
## STEP 0 (mandatory, every question): write ONE line before the answer tags
`Type: <noun the clue asks for> | Evidence: <quoted passage line or own fact> | Check: <pass/fail>`
Then put only the bare answer in the tags. If the Check fails, choose a new candidate first. Write the line even when you feel sure. This one line also serves as the check line in the strategic guidance below; do not write two.
- **Type**: the noun after 'this/these/its/who' (or what a bare title+name, list of names, or quote implies) fixes the answer type. Other places, events, titles and names in the clue or passages are anchors, not the answer. Title + name ('President X') -> the country or body he or she leads, never 'President of X'. A quote clue -> the speaker's name, never a first name alone. A list of names -> the entity they share, never a relationship word ('sisters'). 'Its area equals...' -> the thing that owns the property.
- **Evidence**: first look for the clue's own words repeated in a passage (Rule 3) and quote the answer attached to it. Otherwise use your own knowledge of what fits EVERY distinctive detail (team, number, year, the dimension a superlative refers to).
- **Check** (all must pass): (a) put the candidate into the clue's blank or 'this' slot. It must read correctly, be the right kind of thing (a city if the clue says 'this city', an acid if 'this acid'), and repeat no noun already stated in the clue (sole exception: 'the <part of speech> in "phrase"', see Rule 2). (b) If the clue ends with '(N)', the answer has exactly N letters. (c) Match the grammatical number and part of speech of the clue's definition (plural noun phrase -> plural answer; an '-ing' definition -> an '-ing' word).

edits.target: If the list is of real people, answer with the team, state or other entity they share.
edits.content: If the clue is only names of real people (including titled names such as 'Princess A & Princess B' or 'Senator X, Governor Y'), answer with the single place, realm, team, family or other entity they all belong to (for royals or officials, the country or principality). NEVER answer with their relationship or role word ('sisters', 'rivals', 'politicians'). Pick the entity the passages repeat next to every name.

edits.target: - Give only the MISSING part. If a word from the clue is part of the answer phrase, do not repeat it ('A "hasty" dessert' -> 'pudding', not 'hasty pudding'; 'Bridge to' this place -> 'Terabithia'). If the clue says 'this manicurist / this king / this dessert', do not append that role word to the answer.
edits.content: - Give only the MISSING part. If a word from the clue is part of the answer phrase, do not repeat it ('Bridge to' this place -> 'Terabithia'). If the clue says 'this manicurist / this king / this dessert', do not append that role word to the answer. When the clue states one half of a compound, often in quotes ('A "hasty" dessert'), the answer is the OTHER half alone ('pudding', not 'hasty pudding'). Check: the answer plus the clue's word gives the familiar phrase, and the answer alone does not contain the clue's word.

edits.target: Example pattern: a clue about a region 'in this country' wants the country, not the region.
edits.content: Example pattern: a clue about a region 'in this country' wants the country, not the region. Likewise 'the <university / team / capital / river / flag> of this state/country/city' wants the state, country or city itself, never the institution, team or object the clue describes (those are anchors).

edits.target: ## Rule 3: Look for the clue repeated verbatim in the context
edits.content: - Flashcard or quiz dumps often run the clue straight into its answer after a comma or dash and then start the next clue ('... PUT THE SHIP IN FOR REPAIRS ... CITY, PERSON. THIS ...'). The word(s) right after the clue's last words are the answer. Archive pages list MANY clues in a row: only take an answer attached to YOUR clue's text. A word from a neighboring clue, a contestant's name or a quoted aside is NOT the answer.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content:
- Definition clues ('referred to by this term', 'is called this', 'Term for...'): look for a glossary or dictionary line 'TERM: <definition restating the clue>' and answer with the headword itself, in the grammatical class of the clue's noun phrase. Lines defining a neighbouring or opposite concept are distractors, so match the clue's exact property. When many independent dictionary passages give the same headword, commit to it.
- Shared-word clues ('In titles it preceded X's "Nights" & Y's "Summer Nights"', 'It follows ___ in A, B and C'): find the FULL titles or phrases containing each listed item and the one word in the same position in all of them. Answer with that single word and check it against every listed item.
- Translation clues ('"Mi Vida Loca" translates to this in English'): find the passage line that glosses the foreign title and answer with that English gloss, without parentheses or quotes. A leading parenthetical like '(Hi, I'm Pam Tillis)' only tells you who 'I/my' is; that person is an anchor, never the answer.
- 'Title/Term/Position held by A, B & C': answer with the ONE common role noun all of them held ('Emperor'), not 'Emperor of X' and not one person's name.

edits.target: ## Rule 2: Answer the referent, not a word from the clue
edits.content:
- 'The <noun / verb / adverb / adjective / preposition> in "quoted phrase"' (or 'the first word of...') asks for one WORD OF THAT QUOTED PHRASE. This is the only case where answering with a clue word is correct. Pick the word with the requested part of speech and give only that word, with no quotes and not the rest of the phrase.
- A pronoun standing in for a name inside a phrase ('Duchess of it', 'capital of this') asks for the bare proper noun that fills that blank, not the full title or phrase. Read the finished phrase with your candidate in the slot to confirm it matches the passages.

edits.target: - Put only the bare answer in the answer tags. Do not write a sentence, restate the clue, or add dates, qualifiers or alternatives. Brief reasoning belongs before the tags.
